description:
Confirmed from the report job (.github/workflows/nightly-v2.yml, 'Open, update, or close one issue per domain', about lines 1058-1115) and the runbook (docs/internal/nightly-t3.md 'Issues'): a failing domain comments on every red run; a passing run closes the issue; the next red run creates a new issue; cancelled and skipped results change nothing (the '*)' branch), so Windows 50-minute timeouts were silent. Four domains account for 13 of the 17 nightly issues (durations 5, docker 3, perf 3, linkcheck 2); e.g. durations issue #2827 was closed by a green run and #2874 opened about 8 hours later.
Decision D1 (behavior to implement):
R1 failure + open issue: comment only if the failed-job signature differs from the signature recorded in the last bot comment (store it as a hidden marker in the comment body).
R2 failure + no open issue: if the most recently closed issue for the t3:<domain> label was closed within 14 days, reopen it and comment; otherwise create a new issue.
R3 success + open issue: comment and close (runbook rule unchanged).
R4 cancelled: if an issue is open, comment 'no verdict (cancelled or timed out)' once per run; never create, never close. skipped: no change.
R5 signature = sorted names of the failed jobs for the domain; for docker and throughput-cedardb list mirror-leg and database-leg jobs separately. Keep one label per domain; add no new labels.
Update docs/internal/nightly-t3.md (Issues section) in the same change. The report job stays the only job with issues: write and gains no new permission or secret.
GATE-J (before editing): confirm the report step can be extracted and run under bash with a stub gh. If the YAML-embedded script cannot be exercised that way, move the logic into a script the workflow calls (same soundness review), and record that decision in context.
